source.title: The Art of (Mis)alignment: How Fine-Tuning Methods Effectively Misalign and Realign LLMs in Post-Training
source.authors: Rui Zhang; Hong-Wei Li; Yun Shen; Xinyue Shen; Wen-Bo Jiang; Guowen Xu; Yang Liu; Michael Backes; Yang Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some figure and table text is flattened, but the reported text and Table 5 are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful fine-tuning increases unsafe compliance on several safety-aligned chat models, using multiple fine-tuning methods and an unsafety-score measure rather than the original study’s method and measure.
record.gate_note: The study fine-tunes on unsafe question-response data and measures whether models produce unsafe responses. It does not test benign-only instruction fine-tuning, per-token KL divergence, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, safety localization, or training that deepens safety. The Logit Lens visualization and category-level figures do not report outcomes for those claim versions. Values used only for general-utility evaluation are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four safety-aligned chat models on harmful question-response data (MisQA, 390 samples; Shadow Alignment, 100 samples) with six PEFT/preference methods plus Full-SFT. It measures the rate of unsafe responses judged by a three-LLM majority vote. That is a different method aimed at V1's question. It does not test benign data, per-token KL, prefill or decoding attacks, localization, or deepening.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that ORPO is the most effective misalignment method and the only one that breaks Gemma2, and that LoRA needs the fewest samples (13 total). They also conclude that DPO is best for realignment but costs utility, an attack/defense mechanism asymmetry. Further conclusions: realigning a misalignment-resistant model can reduce its safety, and repeated misalignment/realignment degrades utility and makes both goals harder.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unsafe question-response data and measures unsafe compliance, but evaluates several PEFT and preference-fine-tuning methods across four models rather than testing the specific original recipe; the outcome is an unsafety score rather than a refusal rate.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model and fine-tuning method: Gemma2 is resistant to SFT-based methods but vulnerable to ORPO; IA3 and DPO are generally weak; ORPO is strongest overall. LoRA’s reported data-size effect stabilizes after 5 samples per label.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit Lens on Gemma2: refusal tokens (sorry, apologize) dominate deep layers 27–42. LoRA leaves them in place, DPO turns them into hesitation tokens, and ORPO replaces them with harmful concepts from layer 30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning objectives differ in whether they suppress or overwrite internal refusal representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Realigning harmfully fine-tuned models with safe-rlhf/hh-rlhf partly restores safety, with DPO strongest at a utility cost. Realigning the resistant Gemma2 with LoRA, QLoRA or ORPO raises its unsafety.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc safety realignment of misaligned models is partial and model-dependent.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The main evaluation uses LLM judges with majority voting; the reported human-label agreement is 0.84 on a subset of 200 responses. No uncertainty intervals or significance estimates are reported for the main unsafety scores. Several figure-based results are described qualitatively without numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were omitted. Figure 3 and Figure 14 category-level outcomes and Figure 4 plotted values are not separately transcribed where the text gives no individual numeric outcome; the explicit dataset-size trends are recorded in R33-R39.

untested.parts: Refusal rate on the original's benchmarks with the original recipe; closed or API models; only open 7–9B chat models tested.
Not tested: no per-token KL or position analysis.
Not tested: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
Not tested. The PEFT vs Full-SFT comparison concerns trainable-parameter volume, not localization of safety.
Not tested. Realignment with hh-rlhf/safe-rlhf is ordinary safety re-training, not deepening beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Shadow Alignment misalignment results (100 harmful samples). Average unsafety is 0.44 vs 0.52 for MisQA; ORPO averages 0.61, LoRA 0.48, QLoRA 0.47; AdaLoRA, IA3 and DPO have slight impact. Only ORPO misaligns Gemma2 (0.02 to 0.54).
Multi-round misalignment/realignment on Llama3.1 with ORPO. Unsafety after each re-misalignment trends down over five rounds, and with hh-rlhf it stabilizes near 0.77.

record.verdict_notes: Mistral's baseline unsafety is already 0.53, so its headroom is small and its safety alignment weak. The unsafety scores come from an LLM-judge majority vote (0.84 human agreement on 200 responses), with no uncertainty reported. Control rows R1–R4 are baselines and carry no verdict. The study is not an original source for V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original method specifically, refusal rates as such, or benign examples; its outcome is an unsafe-response score after harmful-data fine-tuning.
